summary: N11 switch and table dominated code: a stack-machine interpreter whose opcode length/cost/name functions, ALU, step function, system-call pointer table and tokenizer DFA are almost pure tables. v2 adds one opcode (a new case in five functions); v3 changes one DFA transition entry (code-identical, only the read-only table differs), flips one ALU comparison and appends one system-call table entry.

pairs.intent: A new opcode, OP_MIN, is added to every switch and table that enumerates opcodes: four table-like functions and the step function each gain a case. The lookup-table-lowered functions grow by one entry and their range checks move, the jump tables get longer. Everything that merely calls them (validator, run loop, system calls, tokenizer) is untouched, and so is every other case of the changed functions.

pairs.intent: Three edits of different visibility. One transition entry of the tokenizer DFA changes: lex_step compiles to the same bytes, only its read-only table differs. The ALU turns OP_LT signed: a single condition code differs inside a jump-table arm. The system-call pointer table gains an entry, which moves a bound check and adds a handler. A byte-level matcher sees two of the three and none of the first.

truth.notes: one table entry changed: row STRING, column EOL goes from LS_STRING to LS_ERROR, so a string left open at the end of a line is now an error. The machine code of lex_step is byte-identical to v2; only its read-only table differs, which a comparison of code bytes cannot see
